messages.author: 6033d3c0e7d242fa
messages.subject: Re: Regarding Spatially-aware k-means clustering and  Spatial shrunken centroids
parts:
Hi Purva,

I'm sorry the spatialShrunkenCentroids method is giving you an error. I'm afraid I would probably need to test with your particular dataset to uncover the issue, since I'm not sure why spatialKMeans would work but spatialShrunkenCentroids would give an error.

The spatially-aware k-means clustering is described in Alexandrov & Kobarg 2011 (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/21685075) but they do not give much help in interpreting meaningful masses. The plot of the centers is just showing the mean spectrum for each cluster. Unfortunately, it does not give much information about the separation between clusters, since it does not account for variation. You can plot betweenss to get a plot of how much each mass is varying between clusters. A large betweenss would mean more separation between clusters (generally) but does not give you information about specific clusters. The withinss tells you how much each mass varies within each cluster.

If spatialShrunkenCentroids weren't giving you an error, the plot you'd want is the t-statistics for each m/z-value, which would give you an idea of the separation between segments for each mass. See Bemis et al. 2016 (http://www.mcponline.org/content/15/5/1761) for interpretation of these plots.

Neither of these methods are hierarchical, so there is no way to get a tree from them. There are plenty of hierarchical clustering R packages, but I don't currently know of any that incorporate spatial information.

-Kylie
